First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -9 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}10 & -6 \\ -6 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 6 & 10\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
